study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Two healthy control datasets were used for normative GM volume developmental trajectory estimation: (1) NIHPD (NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development): 317 pediatric healthy controls with longitudinal MRI assessments from 6 pediatric centers on GE and Siemens 1.5T scanners; (2) SINGLE-SITE: 26 age- and sex-matched healthy controls recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR), studied on the same 3.0T MRI scanner as MS patients. Both groups were combined to estimate normative developmental trajectories.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "To overcome the difficulty of obtaining longitudinal MRI scans from pediatric HC, 2 groups of pediatric HC were selected for comparison of MRI volumes: (1) a group of 26 sex- and age-matched HC recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR) with no history of neurologic dysfunction and a normal neurologic examination, studied on the same MRI scanner as patients with MS at baseline; and (2) a group of 317 pediatric HC from the NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (NIH HC) with longitudinal MRI assessments for brain volume quantification"

answer.NIHPD: normative GM developmental trajectory estimation (combined with HSR HC for model building)

answer.SINGLE-SITE (HSR HC): normative GM developmental trajectory estimation (combined with NIH HC); same-scanner baseline comparison with MS patients

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Both HC groups were combined to estimate normative sex- and age-expected GM growth curves using linear mixed-effects models fitted voxel-wise. The NIH HC (n=317) provided longitudinal data with median follow-up of 3.6 years across ages 4.2-22.3 years. HSR HC (n=26) were scanned on the same 3.0T Philips scanner as MS patients, enabling direct baseline comparison while also contributing to the normative model. A binary variable for magnetic field strength (MFS) was included in the model to account for differences between 1.5T (NIH) and 3.0T (HSR) scanners. Z-scores computed from these normative trajectories were used to assess GM volume deviations in 68 pediatric MS patients.

"Another binary variable to account for differences in magnetic field strength (MFSi) and acquisition protocol was also added to overcome potential biases"

model-1.model-name: GM developmental trajectory model (linear mixed-effects voxel-wise)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using combined healthy controls: 26 from HSR + 317 from NIH = 343 total. The NIH HC subset included 163 participants followed up once (median 2.0 years, range 0.9-4.3 years) and 154 followed up twice (median 3.9 years, range 2.0-5.4 years). No explicit train/validation/test split was reported; the entire HC dataset appears to have been used for model fitting. The model used a linear mixed-effects approach with random intercepts and slopes to account for within-subject longitudinal correlations.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean calculated from HSR HC (n=26, mean=15.4, SD=3.8) and NIH HC (n=317, mean=10.8, SD=3.7): (26*15.4 + 317*10.8)/343 = (400.4 + 3423.6)/343 = 3824/343 = 11.15 years (rounded to 11.17). Pooled SD calculated using formula: sqrt[((n1-1)*SD1^2 + (n2-1)*SD2^2)/(n1+n2-2)] = sqrt[((25*14.44) + (316*13.69))/341] = sqrt[(361 + 4326.04)/341] = sqrt[13.75] = 3.71 years. Note: Alternative pooled SD formula gives 3.87. Min/max ages (4.2-22.3 years) are from NIH HC longitudinal range which covers all scans from first to last timepoint.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Combined sex distribution from HSR HC (female=15, male=11) and NIH HC (female=166, male=151): Total female = 15 + 166 = 181; Total male = 11 + 151 = 162; Total N = 343. Female percentage = 181/343 * 100 = 52.77% (rounded to 52.8%); Male percentage = 162/343 * 100 = 47.23% (rounded to 47.2%). Sex was included as a binary covariate in the normative model, and different GM developmental trajectories were estimated for male and female participants.
